Chapter Four: The Rise of Nationalism and the Decline of Monarchy
By the early 1900s, the world that had shaped the royal cousins was slipping away. The old certainties—monarchy, empire, tradition—were under attack from every direction. Nationalism was sweeping across Europe, stirring up passions and resentments that royal families just couldn’t control anymore. People everywhere wanted a voice, and the old ways of ruling? They just weren’t working.
Over in Germany, Wilhelm was desperate to prove his country’s strength. He threw himself into a bold, sometimes reckless, policy of militarism and expansion. In his eyes, only a united and powerful Germany would earn respect. So, he took risks—sometimes big ones. The German military grew larger and more intimidating, and foreign policy took on a harder edge. Wilhelm’s speeches were full of bravado and warning, meant to inspire, but often they just made other nations nervous. The sense that something dangerous was coming only grew stronger.
Meanwhile, Nicholas in Russia was facing a rising storm at home. He clung to the old traditions, seeing himself as the guardian of a sacred trust—responsible for holding back the forces of revolution. But the world was changing faster than he could keep up. Strikes, protests, even violence became everyday events. And Nicholas’s answer? Repression, not reform. The distance between his royal family and the Russian people kept growing. The feeling of crisis hung in the air.
Watching all this unfold from Britain, George understood the dangers better than his cousins. The British monarchy had survived by learning how to adapt, by finding ways to stay relevant in a world that was always changing. George worked hard to keep public support, presenting the royal family as a steady, reassuring presence. But even in Britain, change was impossible to ignore. Old alliances were shifting, and the threat of war was becoming all too real.
The relationships between the cousins? They were almost completely overshadowed by the demands of their thrones. Letters became rare, meetings turned formal and stiff. Each of them was surrounded by advisers, each with their own plans and priorities. The sense of family, once so important, faded into just a memory.
It was clear now—the age of monarchy was ending. Nationalism, democracy, social change… These forces were simply too strong to resist. No matter how hard the cousins tried, they couldn’t turn back the clock. Their personal struggles, their rivalries, were swept up into something much bigger—the story of a world right on the edge of transformation.
